ddl:
CREATE TABLE Customer (
    Credit_score INTEGER,
    Customer_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Name VARCHAR(255),
    Phone VARCHAR(255)
);

CREATE TABLE Rental_record (
    Customer_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    Record_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    Rental_fee FLOAT,
    Rental_time DATETIME,
    Return_time DATETIME,
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE Credit_change_record (
    Change_reason VARCHAR(255),
    Change_time DATETIME,
    Customer_ID INTEGER NOT NULL,
    New_credit_value FLOAT,
    Old_credit_value FLOAT,
    Record_ID INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID)
);
gold_question: A rental company needs to manage customer credit records. Customers have name, phone number, and credit score. Each rental needs to record rental time, return time, and rental fee. The company needs to track changes in customer credit, with each record including change time, change reason, old credit value, and new credit value, to facilitate credit assessment and performance evaluation.
nl_text: The database name is rschema_0067, and it contains three tables: Customer, Rental_record, and Credit_change_record. The Customer table has four columns: Credit_score, Customer_ID (primary key), Name, and Phone. The Rental_record table has five columns: Customer_ID (foreign key referencing Customer.Customer_ID), Record_ID (primary key), Rental_fee, Rental_time, and Return_time. The Credit_change_record table has seven columns: Change_reason, Change_time, Customer_ID (foreign key referencing Customer.Customer_ID), New_credit_value, Old_credit_value, Record_ID (primary key), and FOREIGN KEY (Customer_ID) REFERENCES Customer(Customer_ID). The primary keys of the tables are Customer_ID in Customer, Record_ID in Rental_record, and Record_ID in Credit_change_record. The foreign keys in Rental_record and Credit_change_record reference the Customer_ID column in Customer. The update and delete rules for the foreign keys are CASCADE and RESTRICT, respectively. There are no other indexes or constraints in the schema.
